seatRig.description: The chase framing every seat's view resolves through by default.

seatControl.description: The structural constraints/reference for live seat camera input.

yawReference.description: What the camera yaw is relative to.
yawReference.title: WorldSeatYawReference

minPitch.description: The minimum live pitch offset in radians.

maxPitch.description: The maximum live pitch offset in radians.

follow.description: The follow camera: with no look input the camera yaw eases in behind the body's heading; any look input (a deflected look stick, a held orbit/steer) is free-look and the follow yields for as long as it lasts. Optional; absent is a still camera that goes only where look input sends it. Needs World — a body-relative yaw already rides the body.

rate.description: The exponential rate (per second) the camera yaw closes on the heading — about 63% of the remaining angle per 1/rate seconds; larger is a stiffer follow.

whileIdle.description: Whether the follow also runs while the body has no movement input. false (the default) is the classic feel: after a free-look the camera stays where you left it until you move.

follow.title: WorldSeatFollow

seatControl.title: WorldSeatViewControl

cameraRig.description: The program a seat's view resolves through while its published mode state targets CameraTarget — null for a world that authors no camera-targeting mode state. Resolved through the ordinary Puck.World.Client.WorldCameraRigCompiler pipeline against whichever body the seat currently perceives from (the possessed camera body — see Puck.World.Server.WorldEngagement), exactly like SeatRig resolves against the seat's own avatar; no bespoke per-frame integrator reads this field.

name.description: The stable name a Blend op selects this program by.

operations.description: The selected ops, in authored evaluation order.

anchorOp.description: Gets the program's Anchor op, or null when absent (an absent anchor starts from Reference implicitly).

blendOp.description: Gets the program's Blend op, or null.

clampPitchOp.description: Gets the program's ClampPitch op, or null.

fovOp.description: Gets the program's FieldOfView op, or null.

lookAtOp.description: Gets the program's LookAt op, or null.

offsetOp.description: Gets the program's Offset op, or null.

orbitOp.description: Gets the program's Orbit op, or null.

pathOp.description: Gets the program's Path op, or null.

dynamicsOp.description: Gets the program's Dynamics op, or null.

selectOp.description: Gets the program's SelectProgram op, or null.

cameraRig.title: WorldCameraProgram

studyToolchain.description: The directory holding the study compiler's glslang/spirv-cross/dxc tools, or null to resolve each by bare name through the ordinary executable search path — never an environment variable.

layouts.description: Gets the authored named layouts. The absence-coalesce lives in the accessor for the same reason Elements's does.

items.description: One named window composition — an ordered list of WorldViewSlots plus a transition envelope, selected for a given session shape by its SeatCount (0 = the catch-all for any joined-seat count). The data-side replacement for a compiled layout switch: an author can see it, change it, and add arrangements.

name.description: The layout's stable name (the view.override layout override handle; unique within the section).

seatCount.description: The joined-seat count this layout composes for, or 0 for the catch-all.

transitionSeconds.description: How long the ease into this composition takes when it becomes active.

transitionRenderScale.description: The render scale (0, 1] applied to every slot mid-transition (a soft dip that sharpens on settle), the compiled director's 0.5f now authored per layout.

slots.description: Gets the slots, in order. The absence-coalesce lives in the accessor for the same reason Elements's does.

items.description: One slot of a WorldViewLayout — a normalized rect (origin top-left, Y down) plus what fills it. A slot whose Camera and Study are both null shows the seat that owns this slot (the next joined seat in slot order); a named camera renders that authored view into the rect; a named study (a WorldViewStudy row) renders that compiled Shadertoy-dialect study into the rect instead — a slot names at most one of the two (the validator refuses both authored together).

camera.description: The authored camera name filling this slot, or null for the seat that owns it (or the study named by Study).

study.description: The authored views.studies row name filling this slot with a compiled shader study, or null for an ordinary seat/camera slot. Mutually exclusive with Camera.

items.title: WorldViewSlot
WorldViewLayout

studies.description: Gets the authored views.studies rows. The absence-coalesce lives in the accessor for the same reason Elements's does.

items.description: One views.studies row — an authored Shadertoy-dialect fragment shader, compiled and rendered as a paired-camera child view a Study names (see the study push-constant/toolchain contract in AGENTS.md and the Puck.Shaders.Study family). This record is the authored intent only — compiling the source, swapping the live pipeline, and driving the per-frame push constants are console/composition-root concerns, not schema ones.

name.description: The study's stable name (a SafeName, unique within the section) — what a Study names and a study.* console verb addresses.

source.description: The study's GLSL source file, resolved relative to the document's own directory (an author's document may point this at any path relative to itself — never the Content-copied BaseDirectory convention WorldAssetRowLoader's asset rows use).

camera.description: The authored camera feeding the paired iCameraPos/iCameraTarget/iCameraUp/ iCameraFov push constants under PUCK_STUDY, or null for the study's own iMouse orbit (the Shadertoy-dialect default).

timeScale.description: The study clock's rate multiplier — presentation only, never simulation state. Default 1; 0 freezes the clock.

items.title: WorldViewStudy
